clue.text: They provide poor accommodation

parts.note: reads like a jibe at shabby lodgings, but means charitable housing for the poor

explanation.surface: A grumble about landlords offering shoddy rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' looks like a verdict on quality; it actually names who lives there, people without money.
explanation.definitionFit: Historic charitable buildings funded by alms gave free lodging to needy or elderly people.

clue.text: One who suffers from depression?

parts.note: sounds like a patient with low mood, but the depression is an economic slump

explanation.surface: Someone struggling with low mood.
explanation.walkthrough: The depression is a market downturn, which hurts anyone holding shares.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who puts money into stocks loses out when an economic slump sends prices down.

clue.text: He takes more interest than you would wish

definitions.text: He takes more interest than you would wish

parts.words: He takes more interest than you would wish
parts.note: sounds like a nosy busybody, but the interest is money charged on a loan

explanation.surface: Someone who pries too much into your affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interest' means curiosity on the surface but the charge on borrowed money underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: A moneylender charging extortionate rates on loans takes far more than a borrower would like.

clue.text: In the clear — not by merit

indicators.note: 'In' tells us the letters sit inside the run of words that follows, across the dash

explanation.surface: Someone cleared of blame, though not because they deserved it.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters are found inside 'clear — not', ignoring the dash; 'by' links them to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To merit something is to deserve it, to gain it through one's own work or worth.

clue.text: Drug addiction in the country

definitions.meaning: reliance on a drug is a state of needing it
a territory governed by another state, such as a crown colony

explanation.surface: Talk of the nation's problem with narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a habit one cannot break and a territory subject to another nation's rule.

clue.text: Ships' prisons and inside are bandits

indicators.note: inside says the conjunction is placed within the word for ships' jails

parts.note: a brig is a ship's jail, so several are brigs

explanation.surface: Pirates locked in the ship's cells are revealed as robbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' looks like it means locked up in the brig; it is the container signal, and 'are' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name outlaws who rob travellers, typically as members of a lawless gang.

clue.text: Put tennis ball into play, grabbing point by deflection

indicators.note: grabbing says the word for starting a rally holds the compass letter inside it

parts.note: to start a tennis rally is to serve
W, west, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A tennis serve that clips something and veers off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grabbing' puts W after the S of SERVE; a point is a compass point here.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden turn aside from a straight course is a deviation, much like a ball being knocked off line.

clue.text: Simply unique

definitions.meaning: merely, just, as in 'I simply asked'
sole, the single one of its kind

explanation.surface: Two words praising something as one of a kind.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as an adverb meaning merely and as an adjective meaning sole or single.

clue.text: Painters may paint it — and in a variety of places

indicators.note: a variety of arrangements says the letters of the two words get rearranged

explanation.surface: Artists might capture scenes in many settings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a variety of' shuffles AND and PLACES together.
explanation.definitionFit: Artists often depict a view of countryside or scenery, which is a classic genre of painting.

clue.text: Pull together on an ash tree

indicators.note: on places the first piece before the next, one following on from it

parts.note: rowers pull on the oars together

explanation.surface: A team hauling together on the trunk of an ash.
explanation.walkthrough: The mountain ash is another name for this tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The tree is commonly called the mountain ash, with feathery leaves and red berries.

clue.text: Induct into office when I answer correctly

indicators.note: putting letters right means ordering them anew, here I with the word answer

explanation.surface: An official is installed once they give the right reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'correctly' signals a rearrangement of I plus ANSWER; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Officials are formally installed by administering an oath of office to them.

clue.text: Organise gay reel with enthusiasm

indicators.note: organising the letters means putting them in a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions to arrange a jolly Scottish dance enthusiastically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organise' shuffles GAY and REEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something keenly and with relish is doing it enthusiastically.

clue.text: Dismissed by monarch and shot!

parts.note: a batsman who is dismissed is out
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A courtier sent away by the sovereign and then executed.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the late Queen's royal cipher. 'Dismissed' is cricket's term for a batsman being out.
explanation.definitionFit: In archery or shooting, a hit landing in the outermost ring of the target is called by this name.

clue.text: Risks of heat in terminals

indicators.note: in says the word for fury sits within the word for terminals

parts.note: the ends of a line or wire are its terminals
heat of passion is anger

explanation.surface: A warning about electrical terminals overheating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heat' suggests temperature, fitting the electrical picture, but here it means passion or rage; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To risk something is to put it in jeopardy, exposing it to harm.

clue.text: Showers seen at the bathroom trade fair?

definitions.text: Showers seen at the bathroom trade fair?

parts.words: Showers seen at the bathroom trade fair?
parts.note: showers are those who show goods, not shower cubicles

explanation.surface: Shower units on display at a plumbing expo.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'showers' as 'people who show': firms displaying wares at a fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Companies that display their products at a trade fair are its stall-holders, the ones who show.

clue.text: Temporary sacking on which mechanic under a car may be working

definitions.meaning: being barred from work for a while, as a disciplinary step

definitions.text: on which mechanic under a car may be working
definitions.meaning: the springs and shock absorbers under a vehicle

explanation.surface: A mechanic laid off for a while, still working beneath a car.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a temporary removal from a post and a car's system of springs and dampers.

clue.text: Exercise in order to be taller?

definitions.meaning: go for a walk to loosen up after sitting
taken literally, lengthening one's lower limbs

explanation.surface: Someone doing workouts hoping to gain height.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means taking a walk for exercise, and literally it would mean making one's limbs longer.

clue.text: Mother is surrounded by excited Latins exhibiting charm

indicators.note: says the word for mother is enclosed by the other piece
excited letters are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A mother mobbed by enthusiastic Latin admirers who find her charming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges the six letters into TALISN, and 'is surrounded by' places the mother inside, before the final N.
explanation.definitionFit: A lucky charm is an object thought to bring good fortune or ward off harm.

clue.text: They can get hot weather

definitions.meaning: heating coils in kettles and ovens that warm up
with 'the', the plural word means wind, rain and storms

explanation.surface: Some places can expect a heatwave.
explanation.definitionFit: Heating coils in kettles and ovens grow hot, and the same plural word means stormy weather.

clue.text: Reliable youngster looking after horses

parts.note: steady and dependable means stable
a boy is a youngster

explanation.surface: A dependable lad caring for horses.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the lad, while its first two words build him.
explanation.definitionFit: A lad employed in a yard to groom and feed horses is a groom's young assistant.

clue.text: Jack and Bill meet us at the counter

parts.note: a jack tar is a sailor, abbreviated AB for able seaman
AC stands for account, which is a bill

explanation.surface: Two friends arrange to meet at the shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack and Bill look like names; Jack is a sailor (AB) and a bill is an account (AC).
explanation.definitionFit: A frame of beads on wires used for doing sums is a device for counting.

clue.text: Island it would be hard to con?

definitions.text: Island it would be hard to con?

parts.words: Island it would be hard to con?
parts.note: put con before the island's name and you get a word for something hard, a building material

explanation.surface: An island whose people are too shrewd to swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Con' is a prefix, not a swindle: CON plus the island makes CONCRETE, which is hard.
explanation.definitionFit: The large Greek island in the Mediterranean, south of the Aegean, completes the hard building material.

clue.text: Join up with the French company first

indicators.note: first says the abbreviation for company leads the rest

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: An invitation to team up with a French firm early on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts CO ahead of UP and LE.
explanation.definitionFit: To couple things is to link or connect them together, as railway carriages are joined.

clue.text: Opposing points in characteristic passage

indicators.note: in puts the compass pair within the word for a characteristic

parts.note: a trait is a distinguishing characteristic
N and S, north and south, are opposite compass points

explanation.surface: Points on either side of a debate in a characteristic paragraph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opposing points' sounds like debating arguments; they are north and south on the compass, and 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Movement from one place to another, especially through a place, is a passing through.

clue.text: They identify trite Latin quotations

definitions.meaning: labels attached to things to name or mark them

explanation.surface: Someone spotting clichéd classical sayings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both identifying labels and well-worn stock phrases or quotations.

clue.text: Poor people take exams outside university

indicators.note: outside says the exams word wraps around the university letter

parts.note: exam papers are papers

explanation.surface: Students too broke to study sit their tests away from campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps the exams round the university letter; 'take' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who are destitute and depend on charity are the poorest people in society.

clue.text: Quiet time for a hotel employee

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical marking for quiet
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A hotel worker gets a calm moment off.
explanation.walkthrough: P (piano) means soft in music.
explanation.definitionFit: A uniformed boy who runs errands for guests in a hotel is a bellboy or messenger.

clue.text: Cheese made with some French backing in part of India

indicators.note: in says the turned French word sits within the Indian state

parts.note: Goa is a state on India's west coast

indicators.note: backing means the French word is read backwards

parts.note: du is French for some

explanation.surface: A cheese produced in India using French ingredients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns the French word into UD, and 'in' places it inside the Indian state after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild yellow round cheese from the Netherlands is a well-known Dutch variety.

clue.text: Unreliable trio let go in opera

indicators.note: an unreliable arrangement is not fixed, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Three performers dropped from an opera production for being unreliable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unreliable' shuffles TRIO and LET GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's tragic work about a hunchbacked court jester is one of the best-known Italian operas.
